name: asc
title: Convert between characters and ASCII codes

origin.description: Convert between characters and ASCII codes.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: Logical indicating whether to attempt to convert the result into a vector or matrix object. See sapply for details.

origin.details: Each string is converted with charToRaw and strtoi base 16, so multi-byte UTF-8 code units become separate integers. With simplify=TRUE, equal-length results become a vector or matrix; otherwise the result is a list.
origin.value: Integer ASCII values for each character in the elements of char. If simplify=FALSE the result is a list with one vector per element. If simplify=TRUE, sapply tries to return a vector or matrix.
origin.example:
## ascii codes for lowercase letters
asc(letters)

## works on muti-character strings
(tmp <- asc("hello!"))

## Use 'simplify=FALSE' to return the result as a list
(tmp <- asc("hello!", simplify = FALSE))

## When simplify=FALSE the results can be...
asc(c("a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y")) # a vector
asc(c("ae", "io", "uy")) # or a matrix

## When simplify=TRUE the results are always a list...
asc(c("a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y"), simplify = FALSE)
asc(c("ae", "io", "uy"), simplify = FALSE)

translation.description: Convert between characters and ASCII codes.

arguments.name: char
arguments.text: A string or sequence of character strings.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: When True, equal-length results become a NumPy vector or matrix like R sapply with simplify=TRUE. When False, the result is a dict mapping each input element to its code list.

translation.details: Each string is encoded as UTF-8 and each byte becomes an integer, matching charToRaw and strtoi(..., 16L). With simplify=True, equal-length results become a one-dimensional array or a column-major matrix; mixed or zero lengths stay a dict. A bare Python str is one element, not split by character.
translation.value: Integer byte values for each string. A simplified vector is a NumPy array; a matrix has one column per input string; simplify=False returns a dict of lists.
translation.example:
import string
from gtools.asc import asc

print(asc(list(string.ascii_lowercase)))
tmp = asc("hello!")
print(tmp)
tmp = asc("hello!", simplify=False)
print(tmp)
print(asc(["a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y"]))
print(asc(["ae", "io", "uy"]))
print(asc(["a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y"], simplify=False))
print(asc(["ae", "io", "uy"], simplify=False))
